rule: Frameworks are not interchangeable; select by size, industry, maturity, risk, delivery complexity, regulation, team capability and culture — and explain why.

frameworks.name: Objectives and Key Results
frameworks.use_when: Aligning teams on a few ambitious outcomes per quarter
frameworks.avoid_when: Team cannot measure outcomes yet; used as task list

frameworks.name: Balanced Scorecard
frameworks.use_when: Mid/large organizations balancing financial, customer, process, learning goals

frameworks.name: Entrepreneurial Operating System
frameworks.use_when: Founder-led SMEs (10–250 people) needing rhythm and accountability

frameworks.name: Lean Management
frameworks.use_when: Reducing waste and lead time in repeatable processes

frameworks.name: Six Sigma
frameworks.use_when: Reducing variation/defects where data volume allows statistics

frameworks.name: Kanban
frameworks.avoid_when: Work needing fixed timeboxes for stakeholders

frameworks.name: PRINCE2
frameworks.use_when: Governed projects with clear stages, often public sector/UK/EU

frameworks.name: PMI / PMBOK
frameworks.use_when: Formal project management, predictive or hybrid

frameworks.name: Theory of Constraints
frameworks.use_when: Finding and relieving the single binding constraint (M02 §008)
frameworks.avoid_when: When multiple unrelated problems need parallel fixes

frameworks.name: Hoshin Kanri
frameworks.use_when: Cascading multi-year strategy into annual objectives

frameworks.name: Business Process Management
frameworks.use_when: Modelling, automating and governing end-to-end processes

frameworks.name: ISO management systems
frameworks.avoid_when: No certification need — use lighter controls
